court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Family Court Appeal No. 29 of 2014
case_name: Santosh Harischandra Reshwal vs Rakhi Santosh Reshwal

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Santosh s/o. Harishchandra Reshwal, Labourer, husband
parties.respondent_defendant: Rakhi w/o. Santosh Reshwal, Household, wife

facts_of_case: The parties are husband and wife who filed an application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act 1955 for restitution of conjugal rights. The Family Court allowed the application with a condition that if the respondent insists on the petitioner residing separately, the petitioner shall make necessary arrangements for their cohabitation.

legal_principles.principle: A conditional order cannot be passed when no conclusive finding has been arrived at.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court could have allowed the application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, in toto, or rejected it, however, could not have passed such a conditional order, more particularly, when no conclusive finding has been arrived at by the Family Court.

legal_principles.principle: A court cannot pass an order that is not supported by evidence.
legal_principles.held: The respondent has led evidence before the Family Court thereby detailing the incident. The Court has considered the said evidence on record.

outcome.final_order: The operative part of the order was set aside.
